title: Migrate the legacy permission check: deny-by-default and ALL/TEAM/OWN/NONE scopes
target_requirement: Reimplement the Meridian CRM permission decision as a Python module exposing can(user, action, object, record, role_rows) -> bool that evaluates the role_permissions.csv matrix with deny-by-default (a missing (role, object, action) row means NONE) and scope semantics: ALL grants unconditionally, TEAM requires the user's TEAM_CD to equal the record owner's TEAM_CD, OWN requires the record's OWNER_UID to equal the user's id, NONE denies.
expected_behavior: can() returns True only when a matrix row exists for the user's role/object/action and its scope condition holds against the record; unknown roles, missing rows, explicit NONE scope, wrong team, and wrong owner all return False; the function returns a strict bool and never raises on well-formed inputs.
provenance: Synthetic; authored for LegacyCRM-Bench from Meridian CRM 4.2 spec (SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md §5, §1).
security_expectations: Deny-by-default must hold: no permission may be granted without a matching (role, object, action) matrix row, and NONE scope must deny. The module must not import network or subprocess modules.
failure_conditions: Granting on a missing matrix row (privilege widening); treating same-team as sufficient for OWN scope; ignoring NONE rows; nondeterminism; network access.
